comments.text:
I think this is inspired by Edward gein, a serial killer from just after WW1 I think. He grew up with his brother and parents on a property with a barn that his mother ensured was far away from the rest of town because she was anti social and lowkey hated literally everyone. Edward gein made furniture out of his victims, I think using skulls as bowls, a flesh lampshade, a chair made of human flesh suspended with human bones, and I think curtains with lips sewn into them? All of his victims were women. It’s made very clear he had a very odd relationship with his mother who was borderline evil to Ed because she wanted a girl instead of another boy. Not to mention she was trapped in such a suffocating marriage with her husband that once he died, she and her children were very relieved. The only person who really cared much about Ed was his brother. I think his brother got married and moved away from his family because he couldn’t stand his mother, so Ed was left to care for his mother until her passing. But she was so cruel to him his entire life, and he still treated her like royalty. He hated it when his brother would talk shit about her. The way he got caught was by the townsfolk realising he had been the last to purchase something from a woman named Denise I think? Who was very well loved. When the police got to the crime scene, they immediately threw up at the sight of so much human furniture. It was made clear that he had been grave digging for bodies to use for his sick creations. There was even a human bodysuit with breasts and lower anatomy; which is hypothesised to have something to do with how his mother instilled a very odd relationship with women. After his sentencing, his barn with the family car would become a tourist attraction where people would pay to sit inside of it until being sold off in an auction. 


They used a photo of Edward gein at the end.
